[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Authentication and Frontend Scaffolding in Laravel: Breeze, Jetstream, and Inertia.js"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Laravel provides robust ecosystems for building modern web applications. When starting a new project, setting up authentication, team management, and frontend routing can be time-consuming. Laravel solves this through official starter kits: Breeze and Jetstream, often paired with powerful frontend bridges like Inertia.js."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Starter Kits"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Laravel Breeze is a minimal, simple implementation of all Laravel authentication features, including login, registration, password reset, email verification, and password confirmation. It can be paired with Blade or Vue/React via Inertia.js."},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"Laravel Jetstream is a more robust application scaffold. It includes authentication, two-factor authentication, session management, API support via Laravel Sanctum, team management, and profile management."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"What is Inertia.js?"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Inertia.js is not a framework, but rather a glue. It allows you to build single-page apps using classic server-side routing and controllers. You build your front ends using Vue or React, while Laravel handles the backend logic, routing, and database interactions."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Installing Laravel Breeze with Inertia"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To install Laravel Breeze with the Vue or React Inertia stack, use composer to create a new project and run the breeze artisan command."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"composer create-project laravel/laravel example-app
cd example-app
composer require laravel/breeze --dev
php artisan breeze:install vue"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Compiling Assets"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the installation completes, install your node dependencies and run the development server to compile your frontend assets."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"npm install
npm run dev"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Upgrading to Laravel Jetstream"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"If your project requires advanced features like teams and two-factor authentication, Jetstream is the better choice. You can install Jetstream with Inertia using the following commands."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"composer require laravel/jetstream
php artisan jetstream:install inertia --teams"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Differences and When to Use Which"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Laravel Breeze when you need a lightweight, easily customizable starting point without unnecessary features."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Laravel Jetstream when building SaaS applications that require enterprise-grade features out of the box, such as API tokens and user teams."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Inertia.js when you want the Single Page Application experience of Vue or React without building a complex API-driven SPA architecture."}]
